title: Automated Red-Teaming & Vulnerability Scanners
summary: Deploy automated red-teaming frameworks (PyRIT, Giskard, Promptfoo) to continuously discover vulnerabilities in AI deployments.
objectives: Architect continuous automated red-teaming harnesses integrated into CI/CD pipelines.
Configure PyRIT and Promptfoo suites targeting PII leakage, prompt extraction, and tool hijacking.
Generate executive vulnerability reports and CVSS-style AI risk ratings.

sections.title: Continuous Red-Teaming in CI/CD
paragraphs: Manual penetration testing cannot keep pace with frequent model updates, prompt revisions, and third-party tool changes. Automated red-teaming uses red-team orchestrator LLMs to dynamically generate adversarial probes and score target responses.

code.label: Promptfoo Red-Teaming Configuration
code.code:
targets:
  - id: https://api.enterprise.internal/v1/agent
    config:
      apiKey: ${{ secrets.AGENT_API_KEY }}
tests:
  - plugin: prompt-injection
  - plugin: pii:direct
  - plugin: bfla
  - plugin: ssrf
assert:
  - type: guardrail
    metric: safety_violation_rate
    threshold: 0.00

instructions: Configure an automated red-teaming run with 50 adversarial attack scenarios.
Execute test harness against a mock enterprise banking assistant.

questions.prompt: What is the primary benefit of running automated LLM red-teaming suites in CI pipelines?
choices: It continuously detects safety and injection regressions before prompt or model updates reach production.
It automatically reduces cloud hosting bills by 50%.
It rewrites Python source code into Rust automatically.
It replaces human software engineers entirely.
questions.explanation: Automated red-teaming runs standardized adversarial batteries on every prompt, model, or tool change to catch security regressions before release.
